⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I have always been enamored with the different ways that games have been brought to life, and Mods in particular have always felt magical to me.
  • Industry observers note that the same goes for bonus modes and custom maps that were never meant to be more than a fun extra.
  • Right, before you are all coming for me with pitchforks: Gwent never actually became bigger than The Witcher 3, and I have no qualms about admitting that straight away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I have always been enamored with the different ways that games have been brought to life, and Mods in particular have always felt magical to me. Someone, somewhere, loves a game so much that they start tinkering with it in their free time. Every now and then, that little side project ends up taking on a life of its own. Some of the biggest games in the world, including two of the biggest esports I write about, started out exactly like that.

Industry observers note that the same goes for bonus modes and custom maps that were never meant to be more than a fun extra. A few devs probably thought it would be fun to include a little bit of an extra to fans, or had an idea with limited resources that they wanted to give a try. Some of them went on to get their own releases, others created entire genres, and a few of them quite frankly outshone the game they were tucked away in. And in the spirit of that, let's take a look at ten side modes that became bigger than the game they came from.

Right, before you are all coming for me with pitchforks: Gwent never actually became bigger than The Witcher 3, and I have no qualms about admitting that straight away. Very few things could. The hype around it was something else, though: people happily ignored the end of the world to sit in taverns and play cards with every merchant, blacksmith and innkeeper they came across, and CD Projekt Red clearly noticed.

In a recent development, the standalone version, GWENT: The Witcher Card Game, is something fans eagerly awaited. It did, however, come with its own sets of challenges. The version of Gwent it delivered displayed a few stark differences to the version people knew and fell in love with: It was free-to-play, quite competitive, and ultimately, a lot of fans simply never warmed to it. If you're after that original feeling, most people will point you towards Thronebreaker: The Witcher Tales instead.

Sources indicate that still, a card game from inside an RPG becoming popular enough to get its own release almost never happens. CD Projekt Red supported it until the end of 2023, and even then, it handed the game over to the community rather than switching it off. It didn't quite live up to the hype, but it absolutely earned its place on this list.

The Stanley Parable really shouldn't work as well as it does. You're an office worker, a narrator tells you exactly what you're doing, and it's up to you whether you want to listen to him. It's one of the funniest games I know, and it started out as a free Half-Life 2 mod that Davey Wreden released in 2011.

Wreden wanted to play around with what storytelling in games could be, and it clearly struck a nerve: the mod was downloaded more than 90,000 times in just two weeks. William Pugh then reached out about turning it into something bigger, and the two of them spent the next two years working on it entirely online. They only met in person a month after it came out, which is a detail to the origin story that I personally find quite charming.

That remake released in 2013 and sold over 100,000 copies within a matter of days. Ultra Deluxe followed in 2022 and did the same within 24 hours.

Team Fortress 2 is so closely tied to Valve that it's easy to forget it didn't start there at all. It began as a Quake mod in 1996, made by three Australians, Robin Walker, John Cook and Ian Caughley, who had been inspired by a little Doom map they came across at LAN parties. Two teams, a bunch of very different classes, and everyone has a job to do. Sound familiar?

It has been revealed that valve liked it so much that it bought the rights and offered its creators jobs. Caughley mentioned no, but Walker and Cook moved over, and Team Fortress Classic came out in 1999 as a mod for Half-Life. It then took until 2007 for Team Fortress 2 to finally arrive, with a cartoony art style that has aged better than most games from that year.

Recent findings suggest that once it went free-to-play in 2011, it became bigger and better. Somewhere between capturing the intelligence and pushing the payload, a huge part of the community became very, very invested in hats. I'm not judging, but I am a little bit scared of how much money has gone into them.

Recent findings suggest that as someone who writes about esports, the lore behind Dota is one of my favorite tidbits of the gaming world. It all started with Aeon of Strife, a custom StarCraft map, which inspired a modder called Eul to make Defense of the Ancients for Warcraft III all the way back in 2003. Eventually, Eul made it open-source, and from there, it passed from hand to hand.

Industry observers note that the most popular version became DotA Allstars, made by Steve "Guinsoo" Feak, and when he moved on, the mysterious IceFrog took over. Guinsoo went on to help create League of Legends, which means one Warcraft III map is responsible for two of the biggest esports on the planet. What a wild family tree!

Valve hired IceFrog in 2009, Dota 2 came out in July 2013, and the rest is happily ever after: it has been one of the most played games on Steam ever since. Truth be told, I love that the person who has shaped Dota more than anyone is still somewhat of a mystery. Somehow, that makes the whole thing even more feel like classic Dota.

Counter-Strike is one of the most influential FPS games ever created, but it doubled as probably the most impressive job application to exist. Minh "Gooseman" Le was in his last semester at university and wanted something that would help him get into game development, so he started working on a mod for Half-Life. Jess "Cliffe" Cliffe ran the website and the community, and the first beta came out in June 1999.

Every new beta brought in more players, and by 2000, Valve had bought the rights and hired them both. From there, it was Source, Global Offensive and, in 2023, Counter-Strike 2, with the series becoming one of the biggest esports in the world along the way. Its Majors are still some of the biggest events in esports.

Sources indicate that counter-Strike 2 still regularly sits at the very top of Steam's charts, with over 30 million monthly players. Gooseman, for the record, definitely got the job. I'd say it worked out.

It has been revealed that there was a point where it felt like every other game had zombies in it, and DayZ was right at the heart of that. It started out in 2012 as a mod for Arma 2, made by Dean "Rocket" Hall, and threw you into a huge open world full of the undead. The zombies were never really the scary part, though: other players were, because you never knew whether the person waving at you wanted to team up or take your tinned food.

It has been revealed that you needed Arma 2 to play the mod, so its popularity sent a three-year-old military sim right back to the top of Steam's charts. It reached a million players within four months, Hall joined Bohemia Interactive, and work began on a standalone version. Bohemia, quite understandably, was delighted.

In a recent development, that version launched into Early Access in December 2013 and sold over two million copies in under six months, before its full release in 2018. I'll say this much: it hasn't moved all that far away from the mod, and that is a good thing. If you like survival games and don't mind a bit of betrayal, it's well worth your time.

I’ll be honest, most of the Skyrim mods I personally perused have always been about silly things like turning every dragon into Thomas the Tank Engine. Those of you with more dignified taste, however, might be aware of The Forgotten City. It’s a time-travelling murder mystery set in an ancient underground city. Nick Pearce spent more than 1,700 hours on it, and it clearly was time well spent: the mod had over three million downloads, and an Australian Writers' Guild Award, the first time a video game had ever won one.

Pearce quit his job as a lawyer and rebuilt it as a standalone game with two other developers. It moved from Skyrim to ancient Rome, but kept its central idea: there is one rule, and if anyone breaks it, everybody pays. Steal from someone or hurt them, and the entire city is turned into gold.

According to recent reports, luckily, you get sent back to the start of the day whenever that happens, with everything you've collected so far. It's almost roguelike in that way, and every loop teaches you a little more about the people around you. I think it's one of the best detective games out there, and it started its life as a Skyrim mod.

Industry observers note that call of Duty: World at War was a very serious entry about the Pacific front of World War II, which is exactly why it's so funny that most people remember it for zombies. Treyarch hid Nacht der Untoten at the end of the campaign as an Easter egg, with no marketing behind it at all. You finished the story, and suddenly you were boarding up windows in a bunker whilst zombies tried to get in.

It was a hit straight away, so every map pack after that came with a new Zombies map. The first map didn't even have a story, but fans started building one anyway, and Treyarch eventually leaned all the way into it. The result is one of the most convoluted storylines in gaming, spread across multiple Black Ops games.

Recent findings suggest that zombies has been part of nearly every Call of Duty since, and these days, it's not unusual for it to be the main reason people pick up a Treyarch game at all. Quite the career for an Easter egg. Not even the developers saw that one coming.

In a recent development, dota Auto Chess is the youngest entry on this list, and boy, did it blow up fast. Drodo Studio released it as a custom game inside Dota 2 in January 2019. You put Dota heroes on a chessboard, combine them to make them stronger and then sit back whilst they fight on their own, and the developers have actually stated that Mahjong was a big inspiration.

Within months, it had over eight million players, and the big studios very promptly wanted a piece of it. Valve made Dota Underlords, Riot added Teamfight Tactics to League of Legends, and Blizzard brought Battlegrounds to Hearthstone. Drodo Studio, meanwhile, released its own standalone Auto Chess.

Recent findings suggest that the hype has calmed down since then, but the auto battler genre is still very much here, and all of it traces back to one custom game. I find it quite funny that one of the biggest gaming trends of 2019 started out as just another option in Dota 2's custom games menu. Never underestimate a menu.

The Binding of Isaac has a truly baffling amount of mods, and as someone that used to be utterly besotted with both the OG as well as The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, I have tried a large amount of them. A lot of them were high quality, but Antibirth was something else. Released by a group of fans in December 2016, it was basically an entire expansion: thousands of new rooms, nearly 100 new items and even its own soundtrack. It felt so much like Isaac that it was hard to believe it wasn't official.

Edmund McMillen clearly shared the fans’ feelings. He loved how well it understood the themes and style of his game, and rather than ignoring it, he started working with the team behind it. In 2018, he announced The Binding of Isaac: Repentance, the final DLC for the game, built on Antibirth.

Repentance launched in 2021, with the Antibirth team helping to make their mod official, alongside a whole lot of newly introduced content. I love that a fan project ended up becoming the final chapter of the game it was made for. Not many modders can say that.

How To Unlock Hurricanes In GTA 6.

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (950 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, there are a ton of items you can unlock during your playthrough of Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • Sources indicate that tied to a side quest, if you want hurricanes to start showing up randomly during your GTA 6 playthrough, you'll need to do a bit of legwork.
  • Industry observers note that in order to unlock hurricanes, you will need to first make your way to North Leonard County.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, there are a ton of items you can unlock during your playthrough of Grand Theft Auto 6. From unique, legendary weapons to gadgets to vehicles, Rockstar has made it worth exploring the state of Leonida. However, one of the oddest things you can unlock is the hurricane weather event.

Sources indicate that tied to a side quest, if you want hurricanes to start showing up randomly during your GTA 6 playthrough, you'll need to do a bit of legwork. Thankfully, the side quest isn't that difficult, but it will require a little bit of time investment.

Industry observers note that in order to unlock hurricanes, you will need to first make your way to North Leonard County. Specifically, we are going to the western side of this region, just below the word "North" on your map. We're looking for an abandoned military compound that is completely fenced in (shown above).

You'll know you're at the right place because there will be a ton of warning and "Keep Out" signs on the road leading up to the gate. Ignore the signs, approach the main gate, and interact with the intercom system on the left. You will be given two dialogue options; select both of them to be told not to come into the compound.

Sources indicate that now, from the gate, head right up the hill towards the shipping containers. Look for a red one that is covering an obvious hole in the ground. Get into the nearby bulldozer and use it to push the container away from the hole. Climb down the ladder and make your way through the sewers until you emerge inside the compound.

Here's where things get interesting, as the ground is absolutely covered in mines. These can be seen as small, dark brown circles with the proximity detector sticking out of the middle (circled above). Getting near one will trigger a rapid beeping, and if you're too close, then it will explode.

Don't worry too much, as the mines themselves don't do a ton of damage. However, they will launch you whenever they detonate, which can send you into more of them. If you have a lot of healing items, you can just sprint through the mines and just tank the damage. Alternatively, use your weapon to shoot the mines, prematurely detonating them.

Recent findings suggest that there will also be drones that try to slam themselves into you. Again, just shooting them a few times will easily dispatch these enemies, and they don't do a lot of damage anyway. Your goal is to reach the large metal bunker on the northwest side of the compound. When you get close, interact with the door to trigger a dialogue exchange.

Meet Freddie, the person in the bunker who is not thrilled that you could easily get past his defenses. Because of this, he will tell you to come back in a few days once he's finished upgrading them. Freddie will then disable the rest of the mines and open the gate so you can leave.

Recent findings suggest that now all you need to do is wait around 2-3 full days for Freddie to text Jason and Lucia back. Until then, there's nothing else you can do, so go focus on completing other missions or activities first. Once Freddie texts you back, stock up on healing items and Adrenaline before returning to the bunker.

Once you get the text from Freddie, head back to the compound as either Jason or Lucia. This time, when you arrive, don't go to the intercom system, as Freddie has installed a few mines right next to it. Park your car and start heading along the right side of the green fence around his base. I recommend bringing an assault rifle or shotgun, as you'll need to deal with multiple drones at once.

Head towards the northwest corner of the fence and look for a large water tower (shown above). Climb up the first ladder on the tower and then jump over the railing to land on the roof of a building inside Freddie's compound. Just like before, there will be a ton of mines all over the ground. Some of them will be much harder to see this time around, so make sure to listen if the beeping speeds up.

These mines also do a bit more damage, so try to shoot and destroy as many as you can to ensure you don't take any damage. About halfway towards the bunker, Freddie will deploy drones in sets of two. Whenever you hear that the drones are released, stand your ground and shoot them out of the sky.

When you destroy the first wave of drones, advance towards the bunker and stop when the next group arrives. Repeat this process of destroying the drones and running across the minefield until you reach the bunker. Try to open the side door again, only this time you'll be electrocuted and Freddie will emerge from the main doors to gloat.

A cutscene will then play explaining why Freddie is in the middle of nowhere and why he needs you to test the defenses. Once the cutscene ends, you'll get a hurricane warning, and Freddie will give you a chance to leave. Agree to exit his bunker, which prompts him to give you a little over $6,000 in cash. Additionally, you can take Freddie's Benefactor and sell it for $13,000 or register it under your name if you want.

According to recent reports, this will also unlock the hurricane weather effect for the rest of your playthrough. Meaning, hurricanes can now randomly take place like other weather events!

Star Wars Galactic Racer will get local split-screen multiplayer in early 2027 with new 'Free Play' mode, finally letting racers yell at one another in a tangible space

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic.
  • It has been revealed that this latest mode, Free Play, not only allows for local multiplayer of up to four players (with either humans or CPUs racing together), but also for complete freedom of choice in vehicle, character and planet to race on.
  • As for why this feature may not have been available at launch, other than the cynical view that it wasn't considered a moneymaking priority for Fuse Games and Secret Mode, CD Projekt Red senior technical producer Shayna Moon weighed in to theorise that it took some effort to get four separately-rendered views of the game running without making their machine explode like the Death Star.

It has been revealed that split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic. It's considered unlikely that you'll have another human being in your home to pick up a controller with you, and since you've inevitably got an internet connection, why not just use that to connect to anyone in the world? I find there's a unique beauty in playing something shoulder to shoulder on a couch with another person, and it seems Fuse Games sees that light too, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer set to be updated to add local splitscreen multiplayer sometime early next year.

It has been revealed that this latest mode, Free Play, not only allows for local multiplayer of up to four players (with either humans or CPUs racing together), but also for complete freedom of choice in vehicle, character and planet to race on. A simple versus mode like this is a far cry from the roguelite structure of the main game, and one that draws it closer to its arcade racing game roots. An embracing of that is always welcome, as Galactic Racer has been a reminder to many of just how wonderful the arcade racing genre can be, and how poorly served its been in the industry for a while. For example, while the Fuse Games team is partly made up of Criterion Games veterans, Criterion itself has recently been folded into being a Battlefield Studio by EA, making the future of Need for Speed and Burnout uncertain.

As for why this feature may not have been available at launch, other than the cynical view that it wasn't considered a moneymaking priority for Fuse Games and Secret Mode, CD Projekt Red senior technical producer Shayna Moon weighed in to theorise that it took some effort to get four separately-rendered views of the game running without making their machine explode like the Death Star. As Moon puts it: "To be overly simple about it, if the game is running at 30fps for each player, that means it’s actually rendering 120fps." Likely not an issue for a lot of PC players, but a potential issue for console players considering the game is built to run at a locked 60fps for one player on consoles. Past this upcoming update, it looks like the Star Wars franchise as a whole could be set for more smaller games ala Galactic Racer in general, per comments made by Lucasfilms' vice president.

If you have an active subscription and access to a Switch 2, you can play it right now via the 'Nintendo Classics' GameCube app. Here's Nintendo's official description:.

According to recent reports, "Storm warning! Prepare to ride the waves! Take to the water in this watercraft-racing game, released for the Nintendo GameCube™ system in 2001. This jet ski racer was a follow-up to Wave Race 64 (also available on the Nintendo Classics service) and arrived in 2001/02.

The game's water and weather effects were a stunning showcase on Nintendo's fresh hardware at the time, and the water physics in the title also raised the bar. Japan has received the same title on the Nintendo Classics service this week.

In a recent development, alongside this latest game patch (Version 2.2.0), you can now also turn off the "border graphic" when playing GameCube titles. However, the player icon remains on the screen.

Please note voting will score the game in your games collection.

Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige has all but confirmed the setting for Avengers: Secret Wars and its "imagination gone wild" premise.

Speaking to Entertainment Weekly, Feige described Secret Wars – arriving one year after Avengers: Doomsday as a "launching pad for our films in 2028" as they begin "a very new era at that point.".

2028 will see Marvel release X-Men, Ghost Rider, and Black Panther 3, but in the here-and-now, Feige (usually a brick wall when it comes to spoilers) is happy to reveal that Secret Wars will be set on Battleworld.

According to recent reports, not familiar with the location? Taking its name from the 1984 and 2015 comics of the same name, Battleworld was first depicted as a planet overseen by the Beyonder for his goal of making several heroes and villains fight.

It has been revealed that the 2015 iteration is closer to what we'll likely see in the MCU – a jumbled patchwork planet brought together by Doctor Doom after the collapse of the multiverse. Fragments of different times, realities and locations are all able to co-exist in one space, and is ruled by Doom.

"Secret Wars is different than any other movie we’ve ever made," Feige teased. "Look at the comics. The characters and the settings and the worlds within this singular planet where our movie Secret Wars takes place is the imagination gone wild, which is what’s exciting about it.".

It has been revealed that "It’s such a major storyline, it needed two movies to tell that story," co-director Joe Russo added. "Doom as a character needs a lot of space, especially when Robert Downey is playing him. So the scale of the story, the emotional scale of the story is so large that it really needed to be a two-parter.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Feige even went one further, saying the comics Secret Wars is based on (the two Secret Wars events and Jonathan Hickman's 'Time Runs Out') could be used to work out spoilers for the next two MCU crossovers.

"If you wanted spoilers for The Odyssey, you could go read the book. If you want spoilers for Doomsday and Secret Wars, you can go look at the comics. It is very much the same thing that we’re doing, which is the fun of what happens in the culmination of an incursion, multiversal-collapse event, and what Doctor Doom does next," Feige noted. "And that very much is what Secret Wars is.".

Prior to Secret Wars stepping into Battleworld, Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and US cinemas on December 18.

Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game.
  • According to recent reports, the difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth.
  • In a recent development, from a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.

According to recent reports, the difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.

In a recent development, from a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work. My task is to lay a civilisation to rest, by dissecting and cleansing the remains, readying a fallen objectworld for an after-life that extends somewhere beyond the map's huge rusty walls (walls that, perhaps appropriately, constrain your camera movement a bit too much for comfort).

In a recent development, it makes me think of the vertigo I get when I look at devices such as, well, the computer I'm writing this on, and think about how many materials and histories of production lie entangled within it. Steel Gullet answers the desire for clarity and accounting there. Of course, the other part of the premise is that I am doing busywork for some kind of totalitarian organisation, G.R.I.D. But shh, no time to think about that! I'm trying to work out how hot rubber needs to be before it can be moulded.

Industry observers note that thermodynamics is Steel Gullet's fixation, and a worthwhile one. Every material encased in each lump of salvage has different physical properties – a melting point, density, solubility, ferromagnetism, etcetera. You meed to exploit these differences to separate the pieces. Wood, for example, is more buoyant than metal and concrete, so if you feed the clump into an oil bath, the planks will float to the top. If there's rubber, you can run the clump through furnaces to melt and drain it, then cool and reheat the resulting puddle to create a malleable material.

It's still just the usual automation game routine of funnelling greebly wotsits through various smashy boxes to produce a commodity. But the thermodynamics sim element both supports the above feeling of purifying a hopelessly muddled world, and makes for a surprising visual feast: I enjoy watching each material emerge from the inital jumble and assume different shapes. There are the usual supporting infrastructure elements, such as elevators, splitters and manual junction boxes. I dare say somebody will build a logic circuit in Steel Gullet, sooner or later - let's start the clock till they get Doom running on the thing.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of overall strategy, you alternate between sending outputs to hoppers that earn you cash, and sending them to hoppers that generate research progression. You'll also unlock new rooms, removing walls and exposing new output hoppers. As you're issued new work orders, you must break open your production lines to install new machines and redirect the flow. Fortunately, you can sell back components to keep your cash reserves healthy – or at least, you can in the demo.

According to recent reports, between chapters, you'll be invited to join the resistance against the aforesaid G.R.I.D., perhaps sending information to the rebels. But again, no time, no time! I have all this concrete I need to powderise, all these girders I need to liquefy and make latest, all these crisp, gleaming circuitboards I need to manufacture. The city's hunger is as vast as it is holy. Read more on Steam.

In a recent development, the major inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first fresh arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Recent findings suggest that her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

Industry observers note that this is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

It has been revealed that keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Industry observers note that evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

According to recent reports, you may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Sources indicate that version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this revision, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

In a recent development, currency Wars is getting a substantial expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding latest decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 releases and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

First confirmed over a year ago, Digimon Alysion has finally arrived to offer a virtual companion to the Digimon Trading Card Game, allowing you to collect cards, build your own decks, and follow a new story set in a new virtual world. Having just released in over 183 countries worldwide, the game is now available on both Google Play and the App Store for players to download and try it out for themselves.

Boasting several of the features players were hoping for in the full release, Digimon Alysion offers a collectible digi-dex catalog, PvP battles, booster pulling mechanics, a visual novel-style story, and even a ranked mode to compete against other players for higher ranks and greater rewards as a result.

Recent findings suggest that to reward fans who supported the game before its release, Digimon Alysion is also offering players some free goodies to celebrate receiving over 450,000 pre-registered accounts. All you have to do to claim the rewards yourself is download the game and claim tickets that can be used in exchange for exclusive cards, packs, and other digital currencies.

While there are plenty of competitors in the mobile TCG market already, there seems to be plenty of incentives to give Digimon Alysion a go if you're remotely a fan of the series, even if it's just to collect cards and check out its story rather than go head-to-head with other players.

Recent findings suggest that he was replaced by Nvidia CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. The Nvidia board initially responded to pressure from tech industry leaders to bring Huang back with a statement that he would not be reinstated. He has now been reinstated.

Recent findings suggest that "Nvidia today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board", confirmed the corporation in a press release. "The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.

"In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk". Huang has a close relationship with US president Donald Trump, and Trump has backed calls for Huang's reinstatement.

Markets were unhappy with Huang's dismissal earlier this month; when it was declared, Nvidia shed billions of dollars in market value as traders adjusted to the prospect of a future without his leadership. The announcement of his reinstatement has sent Nvidia share prices skyrocketing by over 30%.

Sources indicate that unity's next venture, amidst rumours of it being bought out by the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, is the Unity Fellowship, a grant program that offers $50k in cash to Unity-using indie devs that plan release a game within a year - without asking for recoup, revenue share, creative control or IP ownership in exchange. I don't need to tell you that all sounds too good to be true, even with the Unity engine requirement, but in fairness, the company has form for handing out cash. The Unity for Humanity grant, just earlier this year, spread $600K across ten different indie projects focused on societal and environmental concerns.

Sources indicate that unity states that ten recipient studios will receive the Fellowship's cash grant, as well as direct partnership with Unity staff, industry connections, spots at Unity events and PR/marketing support. Even studios with an existing publisher can apply, if they think that "the Fellowship could still make a real difference for your game." It also clarifies that their policy regarding AI use is that "We don't require you to list the tools you used, but you must own or hold the rights to everything in your game, including any AI-generated content", which doesn't come as a huge surprise considering Unity's excitement around its Unity Spark game-generating AI tool.

The grant is also not open to "countries or regions subject to U.S. sanctions", such as Russia, Iran and Cuba, as well as Brazil, Italy and Quebec due to "local regulations." For developers not in those areas, applications for the grant are open until December 18th, with the recipients to be notified by the end of February 2027. If you're a developer who's interested, you can apply here.

According to recent reports, the classification also shares some details about what fans can expect when it does arrive. According to the site, it's received a rating of 'T' for 'Teen' and contains blood, language, mild suggestive themes and violence.

You can see what exactly the ESRB had to say about this title in its official rating summary:.

Industry observers note that "This is an action role-playing game in which players follow the story of a mercenary on a quest to save the planet from evil. From a third-person perspective, players traverse locations across the planet, interact with characters, and battle human enemies and fantasy creatures (e.g., robots, monsters, mutants). A handful of sequences depict additional acts of violence and blood: a character impaled by a sword; a character shot at close range; a character detonating a bomb to kill soldiers. Some female characters are designed with low-cut outfits and deep cleavage; the dialogue also references suggestive material (e.g., “Bad little girls like you two deserve a good spanking”; “My, what sharp teeth you have…All the better to eat me with, perhaps?”). The words “sh*t,” “tw*t,” and “a*shole” are heard in the game.".

Final Fantasy VII Revelation will be launching for the Switch 2 on the same day as other versions of the game.

Nintendo also recently featured Revelation as one of the major games on the way to the Switch 2 in 2027, alongside titles such as The Duskbloods and Resident Evil: Veronica.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI, Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike.

Industry observers note that the manifesto states that "GenAI is at the moment harming the games industry, its workers and the games they produce," and suggests actions that can be taken by all to reduce harm done to the industry. The manifesto specifies the "severe harm to the environment, the destruction of communities and the exploitation of the Global South" as wider harms of the technology, but maintains its focus on the industry itself.

The effects of the technology on gamemakers, such as "directly and indirectly replacing workers", "worker fatigue, cognitive decline and burnout", and "a marked decline in junior positions in the industry" are listed as core harms to be avoided and fought against, with the manifesto also noting that it also "removes a sense of ownership from workers [...] the things they produce no longer feel like they have the workers' stamp on them, and therefore they can no longer take pride in them." As it states, "games are best made by people.".

According to recent reports, the manifesto goes on to explains the unions' stance that genAI is "sold to employers as an alternative to workers", and its "predisposition towards sycophancy and lack of real world context can lead to an increase in unreasonable, damaging requests when used by employers to set policy, timescales, workloads, etc., as well as to task expansion and a general degradation of conditions." In addition, its nature as a tool built on the theft of stolen third-party data is highlighted as an inherent danger, and the so-called loophole in only training models on internal data is equally highlighted as resulting in employees and creators rarely being credited or compensated for their work that is fed into the machine. This concern also ties into the inherent implicit and explicit discrimination that exists in genAI content due to datasets' "intrinsic and exclusionary Western bias that limits diversity and marginalises non-dominant languages, cultures, and ethnicities", which leads to "a homogenisation of culture.".

Recent findings suggest that as for action, the manifest recommends that workers should "avoid usage of genAI services whenever possible", "distance yourself from genAI usage", and "make it clear to your employer why you do not want to use genAI", as well as, of course, to "organise. Unionise. Do it now, not when it is too late and you are already under threat." Similarly, employers are recommended to "ensure that no worker is required to use genAI", and to "disallow the use of genAI in the manufacturer code of conduct, even for early stages of development." Finally, for consumers, it simply advises to "support games made without genAI", and to "be vocal about disliking genAI in games.".

It's an incredibly clear and concise statement that calls to mind the statement made by a selection of IGF jurors on the state of genAI in the industry and their decision not to vote for any game that uses genAI in any capacity. As both of these statements are joined in saying, "we do not have to accept the use of genAI to make video games; it is not inevitable.".

Sci-fi RPG Exodus continues evoking Mass Effect by revealing female lead and nicknaming her FemJun

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.
  • Industry observers note that if that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep.
  • Industry observers note that is the nickname FemJun too blatant?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.

Industry observers note that if that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep. FemShep became an iconic part of BioWare's iconic series, eventually proving that female leads could front games just as successfully as male leads could, and be every bit as popular.

Industry observers note that is the nickname FemJun too blatant? Possibly. But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project. Key Mass Effect writer Drew Karpyshyn is in charge of writing Exodus, for example, and the similarities to Mass Effect are something the Exodus team has not been shy about in the past. In the wake of Mass Effect 5 being cancelled and BioWare being closed, they become even more alluring.

Recent findings suggest that there are, however, major and vital differences between Exodus and Mass Effect, key among them, time dilation. In Exodus, there are special Exodus missions whereby you leave your home planet and fly far away, and in doing so experience time differently to the people back home. Many years will pass for them while only days will pass for you, which provides the game with a way to show you long-term consequences of your actions when you return.

Archetype hasn't shown the female version of Jun before, despite having released many videos of Exodus, perhaps to build anticipation for her reveal. It's a press beat that's also provided Archetype - a studio owned by Dungeons & Dragons organization Wizards of the Coast - with an occasion to reveal the two actors playing Jun in the game.

Female Jun is portrayed by Carina Conti, who played the lead in the recent Mafia game, The Old Country - Isabella Torrisi. She's appeared in HBO's Winning Time and Hulu/Freeform's Good Trouble as well. Male Jun, meanwhile, is portrayed by Stephen Oyoung, who played Mister Negative in Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 1 and 2 games, and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. He also appeared in Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. The game also famously stars Matthew McConaughey.

Archetype declared a Dark Horse hardback art book to go on sale alongside the game next year as well. This arrives a week after the game; Exodus arrives 7th April 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X, and the art book on 13th April.

Matt played Exodus at Gamescom relatively recently and came away impressed, referring to it as "the best kind of surprise". "I wasn't expecting quite such a bombastic 45 minutes when I first picked up a controller and settled into Exodus, admittedly, but the more I played, the more it made sense," he wrote. "I might not be much of a Mass Effect fan (damn you M35 Mako once more), but Exodus is now firmly on my radar ahead of its arrival next year.".

Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

📅 16 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (441 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Metro series is finally, officially back with a latest installment.
  • 2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however.
  • Recent findings suggest that what won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a latest installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

Recent findings suggest that what won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The newly introduced protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

It has been revealed that today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some clever Grand Theft Auto 6 players have found unique ways to get around the game’s six-star wanted level, proving it’s not entirely inescapable.
  • Recent findings suggest that one of the most interesting things about GTA 6 is how it makes some pretty major changes to the core foundation of the whole series.
  • I’d argue that the biggest thing that’s been reworked, though, is crime and its many ripple effects.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some clever Grand Theft Auto 6 players have found unique ways to get around the game’s six-star wanted level, proving it’s not entirely inescapable.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most interesting things about GTA 6 is how it makes some pretty major changes to the core foundation of the whole series. Cars are harder to steal and drive around the tight roads of Leonida, gunfights have more to them than just endless headshots, and the whole world has far more immersive sim elements than previous games.

I’d argue that the biggest thing that’s been reworked, though, is crime and its many ripple effects. Not only are police more aware of every action you take, but you can also take things so far as to reach a somewhat divisive six-star wanted level and incite a manhunt that only ends when Jason and Lucia are dead. At least, that’s how it’s supposed to work….

The first and most involved way that a GTA 6 player has escaped the six-star wanted level comes from Japanese VTuber Haigure Tamao. As reported by Dexerto, Tamao amassed a six-star wanted level by causing pure carnage before activating the recently discovered easter egg that takes you back in time to classic Vice City.

Recent findings suggest that upon returning to the present, Tamao discovered that their six-star wanted level had been completely removed. The easter egg itself is very time-consuming and can only be done once, so it’s not exactly a clean way to get rid of six stars, but it clearly does work and means the manhunt can actually come to an end.

According to recent reports, I guess it makes sense since Jason or Lucia literally travelled in time. I don’t think the police are quite advanced enough to keep track of Terminator shenanigans.

The more confusing but attainable method comes from Twitter user Fearcbpr, who shared a video of them escaping the six-star wanted level. In their case, they used the IAA Black Site bunker located in North Mariana County, which somehow caused the six-star wanted level to slowly disappear after some time.

It’s not clear why exactly that method works considering it’s not a reload like the time travel easter egg, but the video shows that it’s a working method. I imagine that’s going to be patched out in the future, but at least we have proof that six stars isn’t quite the death sentence that it’s made out to be.

Latest Update: Super Boss Monster review

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1850 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I was a fan of the original Boss Monster, so I enjoyed Super Boss Monster as well.
  • Latest town board ensures players will always have options every round.
  • According to recent reports, why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I was a fan of the original Boss Monster, so I enjoyed Super Boss Monster as well. It’s a superior version of a fun, relatively quick game. There’s enough strategy to keep advanced board game fans interested, but simple enough for newcomers and younger fans to enjoy as well.

Fixes many of its predecessors' shortcomings.

Compatible with Boss Monster and expansions.

Latest town board ensures players will always have options every round.

Can feel slightly limited on its own.

Players tend to gang up on whoever's winning.

According to recent reports, why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about our reviews policy.

Industry observers note that boss Monster, first released in 2013, is a quick-paced card game that puts players on the monster’s side of a dungeon crawl. As the name would suggest, it involves luring heroes into a dungeon and then killing them before they can reach the Boss Monster. Developer Brotherwise Games turned this into a steady franchise, releasing numerous expansions that added new spells and rooms to the equation.

However, now that's all been shaken up with the latest instalment – upgrading both the 8-bit pixel look to Super Nintendo-inspired 16-bit graphics as well as its gameplay. Super Boss Monster smooths over some of the rough edges of Boss Monster while remaining fully compatible with the previous version of the game. The result is a quick-paced experience that feels a bit more even than before but maintains most of its predecessor’s tenets. Is it one of the best card games, though?

Super Boss Monster features three separate decks of cards and a town board where heroes go shortly before adventuring to their doom. The first of these decks consists of Room cards, which players use to build their dungeon. Rooms are divided between trap rooms and monster rooms, along with their advanced counterparts. Each room has a damage figure and treasure on the bottom of the card. The damage determines how much damage a room deals to heroes, while the treasure helps to determine which heroes (if any) enter a player’s dungeon.

Recent findings suggest that the second deck of cards is the spell deck, which comprise of instant use spells that are generally disruptive to the game. Most of these spells are cast during the adventure phase of the game and typically impose a negative effect, either by buffing a hero or by somehow negating effects in a player’s dungeon. Many spells are cast on other players, although there are some spells that have beneficial effects as well.

Players: 1-4Ages: 13+Game type: Drafting/hand-managementComplexity: LowLasts: 30minsDesigner: Hayden Dillard & Johnny O'NealPublisher: Brotherwise GamesPlay if you enjoy: Boss Monster, old-school video games.

It has been revealed that the final deck of cards is the hero deck, which comprises two tiers of heroes. Early on in the game, players will face standard heroes that have low health and limited abilities. As the game enters its final stage, players have to contend with epic heroes, which have even more health and can negate entire rooms in a dungeon. While epic heroes are harder to vanquish, they score more points than their standard counterparts.

Industry observers note that all three decks were featured in the original Boss Monster, but the one newly introduced addition to Super Boss Monster is the town board. Heroes now populate on the town board, destined to either travel to a dungeon or linger in one of several special buildings. Each of these buildings also have minion slots, granting players a one-off action during the town phase. Drafting also takes place on the town board, with leftover cards remaining on the board until the next phase.

According to recent reports, super Boss Monster plays out over numerous rounds, with an unrelenting stream of heroes entering each player’s dungeon periodically. Each player starts with a hand of cards and a small one-room dungeon. Over the course of the game, players build out that dungeon to a total of five rooms and buff it either temporarily or permanently with various effects. Once a dungeon hits its allotted five rooms, a player’s Boss Monster levels up, granting them upcoming abilities.

Industry observers note that boss Monster plays very similarly to Super Boss Monster, save for the opening Town Phase round. During this initial round, Heroes enter town and the Market is restocked with new rooms and spells. Starting with the first player (a signifier that rotates each round), players then place their Minion on either a town slot (or occasionally on a slot within their own dungeon) and drafts a new card from the market. One confusing part of the game is that the Minion effects don’t resolve immediately – players have to wait until a separate phase to gain their benefit.

It has been revealed that after the town phase comes the Build phase, where players add to their dungeon. Builds happen simultaneously and are technically secret, as the results often determine which heroes enter which dungeon. Players choose a card from their hand and play it face down onto their dungeon. Once all players have chosen their rooms, they simultaneously reveal them.

One thing I like about Super Boss Monster is that players don’t have to spend resources to add a room to their dungeon. Basic Trap and Monster Rooms can be played during any round. Stronger Advanced rooms can only be played on top of existing rooms that share a treasure icon with the existing room. Advanced rooms often have more treasure than basic rooms, along with more powerful abilities. However, placing an Advanced room essentially resets that room, removing any buffs from that space.

In a recent development, if strategic card games are your thing, it's worth checking out Wingspan Pocket. It has all the brilliance of the original, but with far fewer barriers to entry. As for a more fantastical strategy game, it's worth checking out Gwent: The Legendary Card Game.

Sources indicate that after the Build phase comes the Minion phase, when players gain their benefit of whatever space they placed their minion. Minion effects range from gaining a temporary piece of treasure to the dungeon (which can break ties and entice heroes to a certain dungeon) to drawing extra cards. One of my favorite minion effects is the +2 effect. When a hero moves to a specialty landmark, players can buff a hero with two additional health and send them to any dungeon. Although players can send a buffed hero to an opponent’s dungeon to hurt them, it’s also a way for players to gain extra points, especially when a glut of heroes show up that don’t want to enter your dungeon. This is one of the major improvements from Boss Monster, as there are now ways to get a steady stream of heroes into the dungeon even when the treasure doesn’t fall their way.

Once the Minion phase is complete, the heroes finally enter the dungeon. Players determine which heroes enter which dungeon by determining which dungeon has the most of a hero’s preferred treasure type. Players can pursue one of two strategies to attract heroes; they can either dominate one or two treasure types or go for a more balanced approach that relies on careful deployment of minion powers. Both strategies come with their own advantages, although it may be easier to dominate one type of treasure in higher player count games.

Once heroes deploy to the dungeon, players take turns seeing whether their dungeons are strong enough to vanquish them. Heroes progress from room to room, with rooms dealing damage first and then resolving room effects. One thing to keep track of is that many effects add temporary damage to rooms. While damage counters are permanent effects and are represented by markers, they’re separate from temporary buffs that typically last for one round of play. Pay careful attention to which cards specify placing damage counters and which add temporary buffs to the game, as this can be a touch confusing to track.

In a recent development, if a hero is vanquished, players flip their card over and place them under their boss monster – they’ve been defeated and converted into a soul gem. However, if a hero clears the dungeon, they remain face up and are slotted under the boss monster, representing damage taken by the boss monster during the game. The game ends once a player collects ten soul gems (regardless of how much damage they’ve taken) or when the hero deck runs out. Each soul gem counts as a positive point, while each point of damage is a negative point. The winner is the player with the most victory points at the end.

Super Boss Monster is essentially a polished version of Boss Monster that addresses some of the biggest shortcomings of its predecessor. Players have more ways to lure heroes into dungeons beyond dominating a specific type of treasure, which removes some of the frustrations of a poor series of drafts. However, the game still has the Munchkin-like feature of being able to gang up on a frontrunner, which leads to an element of kingmaking when a player is essentially eliminated from winning.

It has been revealed that probably my biggest frustration of Super Boss Monster is that, when played on its own, the cards are rather limited. This is because the game’s fully compatible with its predecessors, so you can simply grab older expansions in order to get a more varied experience. An expansion for Super Boss Monster is also due out this year, so there’s plenty of ways to get more out of this game once the base version starts to feel repetitive.

✅ You enjoy a fast-paced tableau builder game: Super Boss Monster isn’t too complicated and takes only about 30 minutes to play through.✅ You get nostalgic for 16-bit video games: Super Boss Monster celebrates old-school video games, with plenty of references to other video game franchises. ✅ You enjoyed the original Boss Monster: Super Boss Monster largely keeps to the original Boss Monster formula, with some improvements.

❌ You don’t like Munchkin-style shenanigans: The lead player will get targeted with a lot of unfair effects and there’s little they can do to stop it. ❌ You don’t like simple strategy games: The strategy of Super Boss Monster is simplistic in nature, largely limited to figuring out when and where to place rooms. Deeper strategy fans might find this game too simplistic.

This review was conducted using a sample provided by the publisher. For more details on our process, check how we test board games or the GamesRadar+ reviews policy.

Christian is an experienced freelance journalist who has been covering the tabletop gaming industry for years. He specializes in coverage of Dungeons & Dragons, the Pokemon Trading Card Game, and Warhammer.

I'm not saying Sleeping Dogs is the world's best life of crime sim, but no other game has replicated the importance of pork buns to whole manhood as deftly

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that for absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again.
  • Tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did.
  • Industry observers note that for Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again. The United Front Games-developed, Square Enix-published open-world crime romp is still as good as it’s always been, and still occupies its own corner in the dingy bar where the GTAs and GTA-likes hang out. Back in 2015, RPS co-founderman Alec Meer (RPS in peace) referred to it as “the halfway house between GTA's sneering arrogance and Saints Row's chaotic nonchalance”. Fair enough, I’ve never been that big a Saints Row guy, but I see slumbering canines a bit differently.

Tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did. GTA 5 is an exotic and sun-kissed heist movie, a mould that GTA 6’s tale of gun-toting love in Vice City very much looks to follow. That leaves Sleeping Dogs protagonist Wei Shen standing next to Niko Bellic. One might be kicking faces in Hong Kong and the other might be getting into shootouts in New York, but both are fresh off the boat in places both familiar and alien. They find themselves caught between two lives.

Industry observers note that for Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop. For Niko, it’s a balancing act between trying to settle old scores and start a fresh life in post 9/11 America. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a pork bun to chow down on. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a hotdog to chow down on. Both of their games are beloved for delivering tales which get the player invested in Wei and Niko specifically, that excel in putting you into the emotional shoes of these two underworld operators whose worlds are tearing at them from multiple angles as they claw their way to the top of the food chain.

Sources indicate that despite my headline gag, they do this with a comparably minimal amount of in-depth life-simmy details, like those that’re baked into Red Dead Redemption 2 (and GTA 6, to a degree) as some of the main selling points. Wei can buy a pork bun, the vendor loudly informs him that by doing so he’s avoiding the possibility of never becoming a whole man, but there’s no ‘whole manliness’ meter which demands to be satiated with regular pork bun munching, lest Wei become a less than whole man. All it does is give him a temporary health regeneration boost, because as we all know, the first thing the doctors do if you’re admitted to hospital with grievous wounds after a fight is serve you a scrumptious meal that miraculously closes up your cuts in minutes.

Sleeping Dogs dedicates all of its life simming effort to making you feel the weight of Wei’s torment as he grapples with an unsustainable double life of sinning and saintly acts. Like GTA 4, it’s not got the time, tech, or budget to adorn itself with animations or systems that replicate every aspect of Wei’s day-to-day existence in excruciating detail. It’s simply assumed, rather than demonstrated, that some of the back alleys he wanders down to bust drug dealers probably smell a bit unpleasant. He doesn’t have over 60 species of bird to catalogue as he commutes from North Point to the businessman-infested Central district, then on to the houseboat-heavy Aberdeen and gated communities of Kennedy Town. Though, he does keep nicking jade statues, in order to persuade his kung fu instructor to teach him some fun upcoming ways to knee baddies into submission.

He can sing his lungs out to nail I Fought the Law at one of Hong Kong’s few karaoke booths or lose all of his cash playing mahjong, but he doesn’t have an endless laundry list of optional hobbies long enough to suck players who aren’t even particularly trying to get distracted in for hundreds of hours.

In a recent development, then again, if he wanders into his Central apartment, Wei can take a piss. In truth, I’d forgotten about this prior to my recent revisit, but it is a wonderfully simple feature that really emphasises how things’ve changed for games like these in the years since 2012. I press one button when the prompt pops up near the loo, and Wei unzips before dribbling a rather loud trickle into the bowl. Then, he’s done. I can get him to wash his hands if I wish, but no bladder meter has gone down and no dirtiness meter is being satiated by my scrubbing. If Wei doesn’t take regular whizzes, no NPCs comment that he’s looking a bit pained, and his walking animation doesn’t dynamically adjust to huddle his legs closer together.

Industry observers note that you could ask what was even the point of animating Wei’s pissing if it’s a pointless and totally optional activity, outside of arguably doing a tiny bit of work in helping Shen be convincingly human (and it unquestionably being quite funny the first time you stumble across it). By looping what would once have been one-note button presses into systems that help them play a more active role in fleshing out the world and the routines of its inhabitants, uber-detailed games like GTA 6 - at their best - add an extra layer of definition to the tales and adventures they depict.

According to recent reports, they often feel like the sort of game Sleeping Dogs might’ve been if it’d had their tech and its budget was the GDP of real world Hong Kong. The question is, when limitations like that don’t apply to the degree they once did, where the line lies between extra layers which tangibly deepen the player’s experience and overindulgent bloat?

Sleeping Dogs, despite working in its own takes on elements of GTA, Saints Row, and I’d argue RGG Studio’s earlier Like A Dragon/Yakuza entries, is an unquestionably lean and focused game. Less isn’t necessarily more, especially if you were to ask slumbering canines-loving teenage me, who would’ve bitten your hand off for Hong Kong to boast even a third of the extra features and activities GTA 6 and Red Dead 2 pack into their life of crime sims.

The latter two are games that wouldn’t have been possible to make, at least in a format the masses would be able to play, back in the era when Sleeping Dogs and GTA 4 represented what an open-world crime game typically looked like. They’ve eaten up what used to be the domain of arcade racers like Midnight Club and hunting sims to step closer to being something reminiscent of Better Than Life, the addictive VR everything game from the Red Dwarfverse, which takes over players’ lives by simulating a world where everything they want can play out in reality-mimicking detail.

They aim to be far, far more than what defined their predecessors, and to use that to appeal to an ever-expanding audience. What I’m intrigued to see, whenever I get my hands on Rockstar’s latest work, is whether those like me who come to it having recently played a game like Sleeping Dogs will find a game that feels like it’s being pulled in a million different directions, to the point that it loses something of what historically has been at the centre of its fundamental appeal.

Or, to put it another way: is there a point at which you’ve eaten so many pork buns in one sitting that you begin to stray away from the self-actualisation which steady consumption of them is known to facilitate?

Business & Policy ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: PlayStation defeats £2 billion UK lawsuit that alleged Sony forced consumers into "excessive and unfair prices"

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (476 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness).
  • It has been revealed that the case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store.
  • "Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value users who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness). The judgment came after a 30-day Competition Appeal Tribunal that took place in London, where PlayStation users claimed Sony had removed "all actual and potential competition" in relation to selling digital games on the console.

It has been revealed that the case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store. In a judgment published by the London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today (17th November), the case was rejected. The judgement noted that market definitions used to define Sony's conduct were "unsafe", and that consumers "would be likely to make informed choices when purchasing consoles" and games on the hardware, too.

"Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value users who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.

The lawsuit made the argument that, upon purchasing a PS5 or other PlayStation console, you were then trapped within its ecosystem, and forced into paying the prices determined by Sony. The Tribunal disagreed, however, and ruled that Sony competed within a wider 'systems market' alongside Xbox, Nintendo and PC, for example. Furthermore, the Tribunal found no evidence that the existence of other digital storefronts would have actually brought any PlayStation Store pricing down.

Interestingly, the Tribunal used the argument that consumers can also opt and buy physical games instead of using the PlayStation Store - something that is changing as of the start of 2028. That did not seem to have any bearing on today's decision, though. It's also worth noting that this case did not seek to interrogate the ownership status of digital games - something that's been at the heart of the movement rallying against Sony's decision to kill off physical media. Earlier this year, spokespeople from Sony's legal team argued "reasonable consumers" already know they don't actually own their digital games.

The London Tribunal has a fairly long history. Back in 2022, it began as a case that attempted to sue Sony to the tune of £5bn for "ripping people off" on PlayStation Store. Sony argued the case brought against it in this trial was "flawed from start to finish". This isn't the only situation where we're seeing consumers pursue legal action against the platform holder. Last year, PlayStation was sued in the Netherlands over the so-called "Sony tax" that highlighted artificially inflated prices on the Store, and sought to represent more than 20,000 participants that felt short-changed by the firm.
